land.text: Egypt, to which Muhammad ibn Tughj was appointed governor in 935 and which he entered at Fustat on 26 August 935

predecessors.note: The Ikhshidid page: Ibn Tughj was appointed governor of Egypt in 933 without taking up the post, and again in 935, "while Egypt was at war with several factions". Cliopatria has no Ikhshidid row: its Abbasid 947-969 shape is the Ikhshidid domain (me-08-a notes).

land.text: Egypt (Fustat taken 6 July 969), Palestine (May 970) and Damascus (November 970)

successors.note: The infobox ends the dynasty in 969; the Palestinian remnant under al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah and Damascus fell in 970, the year used for identity.end.

capitals.name: Fustat (Cairo)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Fustat; Muhammad ibn Tughj entered it on 26 August 935 and Jawhar took it for the Fatimids on 6 July 969. Ibn Tughj also governed from Damascus (he died there in 946) and dinars were struck at al-Ramla.

rulers.name: Abu al-Misk Kafur
rulers.note: de facto ruler from 946; "Only in 966, following the death of Ali, did Kafur publicly declare himself as the sole master of Egypt"; died April 968

rulers.name: Abu al-Fawaris Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Ikhshid

correction.text: Egypt with the Syrian governorships Muhammad already held: Palestine (928) and Damascus (931)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Ikhshidid row). Muhammad held Palestine from 928 and Damascus from July 931 (kept by force after the revoked Egyptian appointment of 933), then entered Fustat on 26 August 935. The page gives no area.

correction.text: Egypt and Syria up to Aleppo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Syria is occupied up to Aleppo" in 936.

correction.text: Egypt and Palestine, "Ramla and the south"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 939 partition with Ibn Ra'iq left al-Ikhshid "Ramla and the south"; the 940 treaty "restores the previous borders" with 140,000 dinars of annual tribute. Damascus counted with the north (north of the Ramla-Tiberias line) as the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Egypt and Syria reoccupied in June 942

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Ibn Ra'iq assassinated April 942; "In June, al-Ikhshid reoccupies Syria and reaches Damascus".

correction.text: Egypt, Palestine and Damascus; northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs lost to the Hamdanids

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: on 29 October 944 Sayf al-Dawla "captures Aleppo and extends Hamdanid control over northern Syria down to Homs"; the October 945 treaty "gives northern Syria to the Hamdanids and keeps Damascus and the south under al-Ikhshid".

correction.text: Egypt and Palestine; Damascus in Hamdanid hands until 947

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the pages disagree. Ikhshidid page: "Abu al-Qasim fights Sayf al-Dawla at Damascus" in 946 and "a settlement made Damascus Egyptian again" under Kafur; Kafur page: "secured Damascus for the Ikhshidids (from the Hamdanids) in 947". Damascus is drawn as Hamdanid for 946 as bridging.

correction.text: Egypt, Palestine and Damascus, "southern Syria ruled alongside Egypt"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 947-968, the Ikhshidid domain of Kafur's rule (the shape Cliopatria files under the Abbasid Caliphate, Egypt 91% and Syria 52%). Hejaz is a vassal tint by the ledger; the Fatimid conquest page says the sources do not describe the Ikhshidids as holding it.

correction.text: Palestine and southern Syria under the regent al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Fustat falls on 6 July 969; "Egypt: the core of their rule" is lost, southern Syria and Palestine remain under the regent al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah.

correction.text: Damascus and its province until November 970

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: May 970 the Ikhshidid leader al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah is defeated and captured; "Damascus, which had resisted, surrendered" in November 970.

region.text: Egypt, with Palestine (governorship of 928) and Damascus (governor from July 931)

ledger.note: 935: Muhammad ibn Tughj enters Fustat and founds Ikhshidid Egypt. 'Enters Fustat and takes control of Egypt' on 26 Aug 935 (Ikhshidid page: second appointment 935, entered Fustat August 935 after naval forces took Tinnis); he already held Palestine (928) and Damascus (931).

region.text: Syria up to Aleppo: Homs, Hama, Aleppo

ledger.note: 936: the Ikhshidids occupy Syria up to Aleppo. The page's 936 entry: Fatimids capture Alexandria in March, retaken on 31 March; 'Syria is occupied up to Aleppo'.

region.text: Syria north of Ramla and Tiberias, claimed by Ibn Ra'iq

ledger.note: 939: Muhammad ibn Ra'iq claims Syria. 'Ibn Ra'iq claims Syria. After a clash at al-Farama, they split it: Ramla and the south go to al-Ikhshid, the north to Ibn Ra'iq.'

region.text: the north of Syria, with Damascus, to Ibn Ra'iq

ledger.note: 939: the north of Syria passes to Ibn Ra'iq, the Abbasid commander (amir al-umara). 'Ramla and the south go to al-Ikhshid, the north to Ibn Ra'iq'; the page does not name Damascus, which the researcher reads into the north.

region.text: Syria north of Ramla

ledger.note: 940: after fighting at al-Arish and Lajjun, 'a treaty restores the previous borders, with al-Ikhshid paying 140,000 gold dinars in annual tribute'.

region.text: Syria reoccupied, reaching Damascus

ledger.note: 942: Ibn Ra'iq is assassinated (April) and in June 'al-Ikhshid reoccupies Syria and reaches Damascus', returning to Egypt in January 943.

region.text: the Hejaz with the guardianship of Mecca and Medina

ledger.note: 944: the caliph grants Ibn Tughj's family the Hejaz. 'At Raqqa, Caliph al-Muttaqi recognizes his hereditary rule over Egypt, Syria, and the Hejaz (including the guardianship of Mecca and Medina) for thirty years' (September-October 944). The page gives no date for any actual Ikhshidid control; the Fatimid conquest page says the sources do not describe the Ikhshidids as holding the Hejaz and that Mecca was ruled by the Hasanid Ja'far, so the Hejaz is drawn only as a protectorate tint.

region.text: northern Syria from Aleppo down to Homs

ledger.note: 944: Sayf al-Dawla takes Aleppo. '29 Oct 944: Sayf al-Dawla captures Aleppo and extends Hamdanid control over northern Syria down to Homs.'

region.text: Damascus and northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs

ledger.note: 944: the Ikhshidids and Hamdanids fight over northern Syria and Damascus. The page: Damascus opens its gates to al-Ikhshid in April-May 945 and he defeats the Hamdanids near Qinnasrin, 'and Aleppo falls to him after Sayf al-Dawla flees'; the Ikhshidid page says Sayf al-Dawla 'had taken Damascus'.

region.text: Damascus and northern Syria

ledger.note: 945: the treaty of October divides Syria. 'A treaty gives northern Syria to the Hamdanids and keeps Damascus and the south under al-Ikhshid.'

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 946: Damascus drawn as Hamdanid for the year as bridging. The Ikhshidid page says 'Under Kafur, a settlement made Damascus Egyptian again and ended the tribute to the Hamdanids' (year not stated) and the Kafur page says Kafur 'secured Damascus for the Ikhshidids (from the Hamdanids) in 947'; the Muhammad page has Damascus under al-Ikhshid at his death in 946.

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 946: war resumes at Damascus. 'Truce ends with Ibn Tughj's death [24 July 946]. Abu'l-Qasim fights Sayf al-Dawla at Damascus.'

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 947: Kafur recovers Damascus. 'His military and diplomatic measures secured Damascus for the Ikhshidids (from the Hamdanids) in 947.' The Ikhshidid page has Sayf al-Dawla occupying Aleppo in 947.

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 947: the fight for Damascus ends with the Ikhshidid settlement; Sayf al-Dawla keeps northern Syria and 'recognized Kafur's lordship over parts of Syria' (no year given).

region.text: the Hejaz

ledger.note: 969: Mecca turns to the Fatimids. 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani, ruler of Mecca, reportedly proclaimed the khutba for al-Mu'izz once news of the conquest reached him' (about 969; some sources 969-970 for Medina, 974-975 for the Friday-prayer recognition).

region.text: Egypt: Alexandria and the Nile Delta

ledger.note: 969: the Fatimid army enters the Delta. '6 February 969: Jawhar's army left Raqqada ... May 969: the army entered the Nile Delta. Jawhar occupied Alexandria without resistance.'

region.text: Egypt, the core of Ikhshidid rule

ledger.note: 969: Fustat falls to the Fatimids. '6 July 969: Jawhar took possession of Fustat, after pro-Fatimid agents had already seized the city'; on 9 July he led Friday prayer at the Mosque of Amr in al-Mu'izz's name.

region.text: Egypt

ledger.note: 969: the fight for Egypt ends with the Fatimid possession of Fustat (6 July 969); the remnant of the dynasty holds only southern Syria and Palestine.

region.text: Palestine and the south of Syria

ledger.note: 970: the Ikhshidid regent in Palestine is beaten. 'May 970: Fatimid troops defeated and captured the Ikhshidid leader al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah.' (The Ikhshidid page has Ubayd Allah holding out in Syria until March 970.)

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 970: Damascus falls. 'November 970: Damascus, which had resisted, surrendered. The city capitulated and was pillaged.' Fatimid rule in Syria and Palestine collapsed again by August 971.

region.text: the Ikhshidid remnant in Palestine and Syria

ledger.note: 970: the last Ikhshidid holdings fall to the Fatimids. The infobox ends the dynasty in 969 with the Fatimid conquest of Egypt; the Palestinian remnant and Damascus fell in 970.

wars.name: Fatimid attack on Egypt (935-936)
wars.outcome: The Fatimids captured Alexandria in March 936 and al-Hasan ibn Tughj retook it on 31 March; the Ikhshidid page says Ubayd Allah defeated the Fatimids by November 936. No border moved.

wars.name: Ikhshidid war with Muhammad ibn Ra'iq

zones.text: Syria north of Ramla and Tiberias

wars.outcome: Syria was partitioned in 939 (Ramla and the south to al-Ikhshid), the 940 treaty restored the borders against 140,000 dinars of tribute, and Ibn Ra'iq's assassination in April 942 let al-Ikhshid reoccupy Syria in June.

wars.name: Ikhshidid-Hamdanid war over Syria

zones.text: Damascus and northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs

wars.outcome: Sayf al-Dawla took Aleppo and northern Syria (October 944); al-Ikhshid beat him near Qinnasrin in 945 and the October 945 treaty gave the north to the Hamdanids and Damascus and the south to the Ikhshidids; fighting at Damascus resumed in 946 and Kafur secured Damascus in 947.
wars.note: The Muhammad page puts the Hamdanid capture of Aleppo in October 944, the Ikhshidid page in 947; the Muhammad page is used.

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Jawhar took Alexandria (May 969) and Fustat (6 July 969); the Ikhshidid leader al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah was captured in May 970 and Damascus surrendered in November 970.

certainty.note: No survey lines. The Syrian frontier follows the 939-940 partition at Ramla and Tiberias and the 945 treaty (Damascus and the south against Aleppo and the north), which are cities and provinces rather than drawn borders; Egypt is the Nile valley and Delta.

sources.title: Muhammad ibn Tughj al-Ikhshid

sources.title: Abu al-Misk Kafur
sources.note: Kafur regent 946-966, Damascus recovered 947, death April 968. (The wiki title "Kafur" is a disambiguation page.)

sources.note: 968-971: Kafur's death, Alexandria and Fustat 969, Palestine May 970, Damascus November 970; Hejaz and Mecca.

notes: Cliopatria has no Ikhshidid row; the Abbasid Caliphate row 947-969 (Egypt 91%, Syria 52%, Hejaz, Damascus) is their domain, which me-08-a already handled (verdict adjust, Baghdad core added). Wikidata id not known; left null. The page gives no area for the Ikhshidids, so no sanity check. Disagreement between pages: Aleppo taken by Sayf al-Dawla 29 Oct 944 (Muhammad page) or 947 (Ikhshidid page); Damascus under al-Ikhshid at his death (Muhammad) or fought over in 946 and recovered 947 (Ikhshidid, Kafur pages): the 946 loss is bridging (confidence 1). Not on the pages: Lebanon (Beirut, Sidon, Tyre, Tripoli) and the Syrian coast, Cyrenaica (Barqa), Homs after 945, the 968 Qarmatian tribute and the Qarmatian taking of Damascus (the Fatimid dossier of me-08-c records them from another page), the Nubian incursions of 950 and 965 (Ikhshidid page: Aswan pillaged 965; no territory), Ghalbun's rebellion 947-948. The Hejaz vassal tint (944-969) rests on the caliph's grant, not on a page that shows control. identity.end 970 follows the last Ikhshidid holdings (Palestine May, Damascus November 970); the infobox says 969. Counterparts needing dossiers: sharifate-of-mecca (Hasanid sharifs, Hejaz), Muhammad ibn Ra'iq is an Abbasid commander (abbasid-caliphate); hamdanid-emirates and fatimid-caliphate exist.
